was: BLM Burns District campground on the west side of Steens Mountain (Steens Mtn Cooperative Management Area). 36 family sites amid juniper/sage plus an adjacent 15-site equestrian loop with corrals; general campground, not equestrian-only. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Typically open mid-May through mid-November. Trailheads (Big Indian Gorge, Little Blitzen) at the campground. --Claude
note: BLM Burns District campground on the west side of Steens Mountain (Steens Mtn Cooperative Management Area). 36 family sites amid juniper/sage plus an adjacent 15-site equestrian loop with corrals. Trailheads (Big Indian Gorge, Little Blitzen) at the campground. --Claude

was: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood FO) campground along the Sixes River E of the coast at Sixes; gravel spurs fit rigs up to ~30 ft; popular for salmon fishing and gold panning; self-registration; open Fri before Memorial Day-Sept 30. --Claude
note: BLM Coos Bay District (Myrtlewood FO) campground along the Sixes River E of the coast at Sixes; gravel spurs fit rigs up to ~30 ft; popular for salmon fishing and gold panning; self-registration. --Claude

was: Small Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) camp on Bear Wallow Creek, ~11.5 mi E of Ukiah off Hwy 244. 8 gravel sites, vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage service; Open Memorial Day-mid Nov (snow closes access). --Claude
note: Small Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) camp on Bear Wallow Creek, ~11.5 mi E of Ukiah off Hwy 244. 8 gravel sites, no garbage service. --Claude

was: Small rustic Umatilla NF hunting camp along FR 52 (Blue Mountain Scenic Byway) S of Ukiah; 6 sites, 2 vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage. Short access road is rough but passable; open Memorial Day-mid Nov, closed only by snow. --Claude
note: Small rustic Umatilla NF hunting camp along FR 52 (Blue Mountain Scenic Byway) S of Ukiah; 2 vault toilets, no garbage. Short access road is rough but passable. --Claude

was: Clackamas County park on Clear Creek ~5 mi south of Estacada; 75 sites, 60 with water/electric hookups (sites 28-37 and 71-75 are tent-only), free hot showers, swim area, 2.5 mi of trails. Open May 1-Sep 30, reservable at least 3 days ahead (no minimum stay for a single site; Clackamas County camping rules, 2026-10-12). --Claude
note: Clackamas County park on Clear Creek ~5 mi south of Estacada; 75 sites, 60 with water/electric hookups (sites 28-37 and 71-75 are tent-only), free hot showers, swim area, 2.5 mi of trails. --Claude

was: Small commercial RV park at 40254 OR-86 near Richland in the Eagle Valley (Pine Valley area of Baker County). 40 sites, ~25 pull-throughs, 25 full hookups (electric/water/sewer), big-rig friendly, showers, restrooms, laundry, fish-cleaning station. Reserve by phone. Camper-reported rate: $29 a night for full hookups (Campendium, May and July 2025). --Claude
note: Small commercial RV park at 40254 OR-86 near Richland in the Eagle Valley (Pine Valley area of Baker County). ~25 pull-throughs, 25 full hookups (electric/water/sewer), big-rig friendly, restrooms, fish-cleaning station. Reserve by phone. --Claude

was: 34-site campground on a rise above Wild Horse Reservoir; pull-through sites accommodate large RVs, each with camp pad, shade and fire pit; Loop 2's sites have water and electric hookups (the booking site and Nevada State Parks' fee page, 2026-10-12), Loop 1's none; restrooms/showers year-round, dump station + water faucets in summer. Reservable via ReserveNevada. --Claude
note: 34-site campground on a rise above Wild Horse Reservoir; pull-through sites accommodate large RVs, each with camp pad, shade and fire pit; restrooms/showers year-round, dump station + water faucets in summer. Reservable via ReserveNevada. --Claude

was: Small primitive Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at the historic town of Jarbidge (~6,350 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon, NE Nevada; a handful of sites best for small/medium rigs (~22-24 ft, comparable to nearby Sawmill). Open ~June-Oct once the canyon road clears. Reached via the long graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

Reached via the long graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

was: Small rustic Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely Ranger District) campground ~30 mi west of Ely, then 9.5 mi in on graded gravel NFSR-405. 5 dispersed-style sites along the White River with picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Open roughly late May through mid-October. Reviewers note lots of flat ground; graded gravel access. --Claude

was: Kaibab NF (North Kaibab RD), on AZ-67 ~7 mi N of the Grand Canyon North Rim entrance (~8,800 ft) beside DeMotte Park meadow. 38 single sites in two loops, limited potable water (no RV-tank fills). Half reservable via recreation.gov, half FCFS; mid-May-mid-Oct (road closed in winter). --Claude
note: Kaibab NF (North Kaibab RD), on AZ-67 ~7 mi N of the Grand Canyon North Rim entrance (~8,800 ft) beside DeMotte Park meadow. 38 single sites in two loops, limited potable water (no RV-tank fills). Half reservable via recreation.gov, half FCFS. --Claude

was: Apache-Sitgreaves NF designated dispersed camping along Forest Road 9350, a ~2-mi dirt spur off well-graded FR 300 (Rim Road) atop the Mogollon Rim near Heber. ~42 primitive marked sites spread over ~1.25 mi, many with rim views; two vault toilets near the Carr Lake trailhead, metal fire rings. Open roughly May-Nov (impassable after snowfall). Some sites sit near a ~200-ft rim drop-off. --Claude

Some sites sit near a ~200-ft rim drop-off. --Claude

was: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Black Mesa RD) at the Mogollon Rim edge on FR-300, ~1 mi off SR-260, at ~7,540 ft; known for 100-mile rim views. 26 sites (1-13 FCFS, 14-26 reservable online). Woods Canyon Lake ~3 mi. Open ~mid-May through Labor Day weekend. --Claude

was: Coronado NF (Santa Catalina RD) campground at ~4,300 ft on the Catalina Hwy up Mt Lemmon, ~10 mi NE of Tucson. 37 sites off paved roads, 2WD/low-clearance accessible; no hookups, no potable water. Trailers/RVs listed to 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig — a few of the larger sites fit). Open Nov 1–early May (low-elevation winter site). Reservable online. --Claude

was: Prescott NF, on the banks of Wolf Creek south of Prescott. 20 CCC-built sites with tables and fire rings; no hookups, no drinking water, vault toilets. Open Memorial Day weekend through Oct 31. Sites accommodate trailers ~22-40 ft; graded-dirt/FR-97 access. (Temporarily closed for bear activity at time of research.) --Claude

was: City of Prescott lakeside park in the Granite Dells on Watson Lake; 35 campsites (19 reservable, remainder first-come, first-served), tent/RV, restrooms, picnic table/fire pit/grill each site. Open ~1st weekend of April through 1st weekend of October, Thu-Mon nights only. --Claude
note: City of Prescott lakeside park in the Granite Dells on Watson Lake; 35 campsites (19 reservable, remainder first-come, first-served), tent/RV, restrooms, picnic table/fire pit/grill each site. --Claude

was: Small family-owned RV park on historic Route 66 in Joseph City, open year-round. ~30 sites, gravel level pull-throughs with full hookups (30/50 amp), water/sewer, dump station; geared to overnighters and short stays. Satellite shows a short RV row off Main St just north of I-40. Camper-reported rate: $40 a night in May 2026, $35 in August 2025 (Campendium). --Claude
note: Small family-owned RV park on historic Route 66 in Joseph City. Gravel level pull-throughs with full hookups (30/50 amp), water/sewer; geared to overnighters and short stays. Satellite shows a short RV row off Main St just north of I-40. --Claude

was: Sunrise RV Park at the White Mountain Apache Tribe's Sunrise Park Resort in the White Mountains (~2810 m), off Hwy 273 near Sunrise Lake. 16 dry (no-hookup) drive-in tent/RV/trailer spots; potable water and port-a-johns throughout, tables and fire pits at most sites. Permits bought at the Sunrise General Store or Park Lodge (no online booking). Tribal land. --Claude
note: Sunrise RV Park at the White Mountain Apache Tribe's Sunrise Park Resort in the White Mountains (~2810 m), off Hwy 273 near Sunrise Lake. 16 dry (no-hookup) drive-in tent/RV/trailer spots; potable water and port-a-johns throughout, tables and fire pits at most sites. Tribal land. --Claude

was: Off-grid desert RV park at 50875 Ave 75 E, Salome (La Paz County), open Oct 1-Apr 30. ~40 large spread-out dry-camp sites, no on-site electric; water available limited afternoon hours, honey-wagon tank drainage, showers/laundry/restrooms. Takes daily overnighters as well as weekly/monthly/yearly snowbird stays; genuine drive-in transient RV camping. Camper-reported rate: $25 a night from 2025 (Campendium, January 2025). --Claude

was: Arizona State Parks & Trails campground at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains north of Tucson. 120 sites (Loops A and B) with 20/30/50-amp electric and water; no length limit on RVs. Reservable online. --Claude
note: Arizona State Parks & Trails campground at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains north of Tucson. No length limit on RVs. Reservable online. --Claude

was: San Diego County desert park in the Anza-Borrego area with natural hot springs. ~140 sites across several loops: full-hookup, partial-hookup, and no-hookup RV/trailer sites plus tent sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station. Seasonally operated (open ~Labor Day to Memorial Day; closed summer heat). Reservable online through San Diego County Parks. --Claude
note: San Diego County desert park in the Anza-Borrego area with natural hot springs. ~140 sites across several loops: full-hookup, partial-hookup, and no-hookup RV/trailer sites plus tent sites. Reservable online through San Diego County Parks. --Claude

was: Two RV lots on the Del Mar Fairgrounds (22nd District Agricultural Association), minutes from the beach: Surf & Turf RV Park (60 sites) and the fairgrounds' own RV lot (58 spaces), all back-in with full hookups.  Restrooms and laundry.  Daily and weekly stays, booked up to 2 months ahead, 21 nights a calendar year at most.  Closed in summer for the San Diego County Fair and the racing season. --Claude

was: PG&E-operated campground on the wooded west shore of Lake Almanor (Rocky Point peninsula near Canyon Dam); ~130 drive-in forest sites, sandy beach/day-use nearby. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude
